- The event is identified as the **34th 24 Hours of Le Mans** and took place on 18–19 June 1966[§ 1].  
- The race was the seventh round of the **1966 World Sportscar Championship season**[§ 1].  
- It was the **first overall win at Le Mans for the Ford GT40** (Mk II) and the first win for an American constructor at a major European race since the 1921 French Grand Prix[§ 1].  
- The Ford GT40 Mk II had been developed and improved with wind‑tunnel work, better brakes, handling and engine tuning[§ 1].  
- The GT40’s 7‑litre NASCAR‑derived engine produced about 550 bhp (registered as 485 hp) in racing trim[§ 1].  
- The **driver Ken Miles** is highlighted as a key figure for the Ford GT40 effort: he and Denny Hulme were a co‑driving pair in the winning Ford GT40 Mk II[§ 5.1]; Miles famously had a door that **slammed onto his helmet on the first lap**, requiring a pit stop to fix the door[§ 5.1].  
- The **2004** television movie *Ford v Ferrari* is referenced as an “ironic” summary of the story that began in 1966[§ 7].  
- In the same race, **McLaren and Amon** were the drivers of the car that ultimately crossed the line at the top of the board, but an “ACo photo finish” rule removed them from the top spot in favour of the McLaren/Amon pair; they were declared the race winners after the ACO review[§ 5.9].
